newsitem.title: CANADA: Trans Quebec files Sable gas pipeline proposal.
newsitem.headline: Trans Quebec files Sable gas pipeline proposal.

text.p: Gas pipeline firm Trans Quebec & Maritimes, co-owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, said on Friday it filed its preliminary submission for a C$1 billion pipeline expansion in Atlantic Canada.

The proposal, submitted to Canada's National Energy Board, is competing with Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline Ltd's plan to link the Sable Island natural gas fields off Nova Scotia to Northeast U.S. markets.
Under the TQM proposal, its pipeline would be expanded in Quebec, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia to link Sable reserves to Canada's existing pipeline infrastructure.
"We believe this project provides numerous advantages, including a competitive toll to the Maritimes and Boston markets," TransCanada vice-president Wayne Lunt said in a statement.
"In addition, the system can be constructed with no impact on TransCanada's eastern zone toll."
The project would include a 309 km extension of the TQM line to Edmundston, New Brunswick from Saint-Nicolas, Quebec and a 669 km line to Edmundston from Goldboro, Nova Scotia.
It would be owned by a new entity called TransMaritimes Gas Transmission, made up initially of TransCanada and Gaz Metropolitain, the companies said.

Under the proposal, Sable gas would be delivered to new markets in eastern Canada and the Northeast U.S. via existing pipelines and a TQM connection to the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, which is slated to be in service by November 1998, TQM said.
TQM said its proposal was is similar to an extension that was approved by the NEB in 1981 but never built.

It said it expected to file complete applications by the end of the summer and environmental assessments and public information sessions were already under way. The system could be in service by November 1999, in line with the Sable development schedule.

Competing Maritimes & Northeast, whose major owners are Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp, said earlier Friday it struck a precedent agreement to ship gas on its proposed line to utility Nova Scotia Power Inc.
